record.original_question: Let μ be a non-negative finite Borel measure on R^3 representing an extended nuclear charge distribution, with total charge μ(R^3) ≤ 1. Consider the Dirac-Coulomb operator D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}, where D0 is the free Dirac operator and μ * |x|^{-1} is the electrostatic potential generated by μ. Denote by λ1(D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}) the lowest eigenvalue of this operator in the spectral gap (-1, 1). Is this eigenvalue always minimized, among all such charge distributions with the same total charge, when the entire charge is concentrated at one point, so that λ1(D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}) ≥ λ1(D0 - μ(R^3)/|x|) = sqrt(1 - μ(R^3)^2)?

evidence.quote: Eigenvalues in the gap (-1, 1) physically correspond to stationary states of the relativistic electron. Therefore it seems natural to expect that the lowest eigenvalue in (-1, 1) will again be minimized for the Dirac measure μ(R^3)δ0, like in the Schrödinger case (3).

Conjecture 1 (General charges [13, 14]). For any non-negative Borel measure μ such that μ(R^3) ≤ 1, the lowest eigenvalue in the gap (-1, 1) satisfies λ1(D0 - μ * 1/|x|) ≥ λ1(D0 - μ(R^3)/|x|) = √(1 - μ(R^3)^2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D_0 = -i\alpha\cdot\nabla + \beta$ be the free Dirac operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3;\mathbb{C}^4)$, where $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\beta$ are the standard $4\times 4$ Dirac matrices (so that $D_0$ is self-adjoint with spectrum $(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$). For a non-negative finite Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$, define the electrostatic potential $V_\mu(x) = (\mu * |\cdot|^{-1})(x) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |x-y|^{-1}\,d\mu(y)$, and consider the Dirac–Coulomb operator $D_\mu := D_0 - V_\mu$, defined via its distinguished self-adjoint extension whenever $\mu(\mathbb{R}^3)\le 1$. Let $\lambda_1(D_\mu)$ denote the lowest eigenvalue of $D_\mu$ in the spectral gap $(-1,1)$ (when it exists). 

Prove or disprove: for every non-negative finite Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with $\mu(\mathbb{R}^3) \le 1$,
$$\lambda_1\!\left(D_0 - \mu * |x|^{-1}\right) \;\ge\; \lambda_1\!\left(D_0 - \frac{\mu(\mathbb{R}^3)}{|x|}\right) \;=\; \sqrt{1 - \mu(\mathbb{R}^3)^2},$$
i.e., the lowest gap eigenvalue is minimized, at fixed total charge, when the entire charge is concentrated at a single point.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open in general. Esteban, Lewin, and Séré (Proc. London Math. Soc., 2021) proved partial results: for total charges below a critical value, an optimal minimizing measure exists and is concentrated on a compact set of Lebesgue measure zero, but the full claim that this minimizer is a single Dirac mass (giving the bound $\sqrt{1-\mu(\mathbb{R}^3)^2}$) has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Dirac-Coulomb operators with general charge distribution. II. The lowest eigenvalue
status_evidence.snippet: For all masses below a critical value, an optimal measure giving the lowest possible eigenvalue exists and concentrates on a compact set of Lebesgue measure zero.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: existence of an optimal concentrated minimizing measure, but not proven to be a Dirac mass.

status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 1 (General charges). For any non-negative Borel measure μ such that μ(R^3) ≤ 1, the lowest eigenvalue in the gap (-1, 1) satisfies λ1(D0 - μ * 1/|x|) ≥ √(1 - μ(R^3)^2).
status_evidence.claim: The statement is presented as an open conjecture.
